Welcome to the 2017 Draft introductions. You will likely soon be receiving some lengthy write up by one of our resident experts (BananaGoop, that_guy_u_kno), so I'll be just briefly going over the basic aspects of our drafted players. Hopefully, this will give y'all a better understanding of why we drafted each player, and what they offer to the Panthers.

Round 1, Pick 8

Christian McCaffrey, RB

5'11", 202 lbs

McCaffrey, or now known as CMC by the community, is a dangerous prospect that adds a variety of usages to the Panthers. While we have lately relied on just slamming JStew into the defense for his usual 3-4 yards per carry, CMC adds a slippery element we haven't had since the minuscule Deangelo Williams. While he is adapt at running between the tackles, a play we love using quite frequently, CMC is capable of squirming between the big defensive fronts and running down decent yardage into the 3rd level. Another great aspect of his is his ability to play pass catcher as needed, either from out of the back or if lined up from the slot. His route running finally gives us a receiver who can create separation and find plenty of YAC. And the biggest addition to our team is his return ability. We have historically sat in the bottom of the league for returns and special teams play, so he adds an instant upgrade to our weakest unit.

Round 2, Pick 40

Curtis Samuel, WR

5'11", 198 lbs

Every year, Gettleman makes a pick that we not only question but actually makes us curse out loud. Curtis Samuel is this. Many thought he was a redundant pick, pretty much a lower end version of CMC. Except, Curtis is quite the opposite. While CMC is a RB who can receive, Curtis is actually a WR who can rush. Expect Curtis to primarily line up in the slot, but he adds the abilities to come to the back for some rushing, or even line up further out wide. His 4.31 40 speed pretty much gives us a speed replacement for Ginn, plus one important detail, Curtis can actually catch. The combination of CMC and Curtis significantly increases the speed of our offense, plus gives us the capability to throw the ball up for some yards after the catch.

Round 2, Pick 64

Taylor Moton, OT

6'5", 330 lbs

It's no secret we have almost no answer in the event of injury to one of our 2 penned-in starting tackles, Matt Kalil and Daryl Williams. While the coaches are confident about Oher's status, we do not yet have a definite answer as to whether he will actually play this season. Moton is probably the most ready tackle we could grab at 64. Whether Williams is hurt or replacing a hurt Kalil, Moton is pretty much our answer to step in. Round 3, Pick 77

Daeshon Hall, DE

6'5", 265 lbs

Our defensive line is oooolllldddd. Yes, it's an exaggeration, but our starting DEs are likely the 30-year-old Charles Johnson and 29-year-old Mario Addison. Ealy, our youngest DE, is now off to the Patriots, so Daeshon adds the youth we were suddenly in need of. The interesting thing about Hall is his stock actually suffered due to another player. Playing for A&M, Hall was consistently overshadowed by his partner-in-crime, Myles Garrett. When Garrett was pretty much eating up double teams, Hall managed to feast at times. Luckily, he enters a defensive line where his defensive tackles both require double teams, giving him many more opportunities for one on ones. He will likely play rotational to give our starters rest while he develops over the next year.

Round 5, Pick 152

Corn Elder, CB

5'10", 187 lbs

This one has been touted by /u/BananaGoop, so you know he's happy about this pick. Claimed to be "undersized", Elder plays much larger than he really is. He also has the best name of all our picks. Elder is a corner who plays the zone really well and has actually shut down his side of the field many times, due to his athleticism and nose for the ball. He is also an amazing tackler, and can play both slot and outside. Given what Wilks and Co. has done with corners with limited athleticism (Bosh Borman), Elder gives the coaches a very desirable canvas to work with.

Round 6, Pick 192

Alex Armah, FB/DE/LB/TE/Whatever you want him to be

6'2", 253 lbs

I kid, but it is amazing what we can use this guy for. Most likely, he will be battling Devon "Rockhead" as our lead blocking fullback. He is capable of running lead in zone rushing offenses, like what we run, and can give us the ability to push CMC further for more yardage, or at least help prevent JStew from getting hit 5 yards behind the line.

Round 7, Pick 233

Harrison Butker, K

6'4", 200 lbs

Finally, some competition for Gano. We all loved Gano, but he's really shown his lost luster last season, missing kicks in games where we lost by 3 or fewer points. While Butker will likely not make the team, despite having some impressive numbers throughout college, this pick will put the fear of God into Gano, and push him to actually turn himself around.
